title: iwf-hardcore
label: Hades

won.source: reconstructed from the surviving 1998 show recaps (no IWF title-history ledger survives)

how: The belt was announced from the ring as “a legit title” mid-show by the fed's president — a beat the crew would repeat almost exactly when the UWF legitimized its own THC. First holder: Hades, who beat Crow — the mentor of the recently-deceased Carnage — for it.
note: Holder at the end of the surviving IWF window.

conflict.note: The title record and the wing's own index both record Hades as the belt's first holder, defeating Crow. The served show recap itself (promotions/iwf/the wing's own served documents reads, blow-by-blow: “...in the 20th minute...Crow hit the crows nest sending Hades through a table and to the mat...new Hardcore Champion”. Which reads as CROW winning, not Hades. The recorded holder here is Hades; the recap's own contradictory text is preserved rather than silently resolved.

title: iwf-north-american
label: Coma

won.source: reconstructed from the surviving 1998 show recaps (no IWF title-history ledger survives)

how: Leader of the stable Crash Team — credited as a four- or five-time North American Champion, the belt's defining figure. Defended it against Rob Williams in the Christmas Clash '98 main event.
note: Holder at the end of the surviving IWF window. The individual reigns inside Coma's “4x/5x” run are not separable from the surviving recaps — the record attests the count, not the order. A second, later-hosted source (uwf.rpcommunity.com/titles/nahistory.htm, captured 26 Jul 2007, rpcommunity mine) carries a bare IWF North American holder list with no dates or venues, in this order: Grim Reaper, Joseph 'Coma' Rosso, Rob Williams, Lew Spectre, Curt Raines, Bob Charlie, Cage — a genuine, independent ordering clue, but undated and not a reign-by-reign ledger, so it isn't split into new rows here rather than inventing dates the source doesn't give.

title: iwf-tag-team
label: “Omega” — Curt Raines & Scott Maestol

won.source: reconstructed from the surviving 1998 show recaps (no IWF title-history ledger survives)

how: Reigning champions into the Oct-Dec 1998 window; per the fed's own 1998 Slammy Awards retrospective (IWF Additions/1998.htm), "Curt Raines and Scott Maestol became the World Tag Team Champions by defeating the Crash Team at the King of the Ring Pay Per View in July" — they "defended there belts against everyone... and never lost them," until "Scott became injured, the two had to forfeit the titles."
note: Holder at the end of the surviving IWF window. Curt Raines carried on to become the GIWF's second World Champion. OMEGA CHECK: that Scott Maestol was the partner of Curt Raines in Omega, verified directly against the fed's own 1998 retrospective — confirmed, and already fully modeled on this row (holder: omega, members Curt Raines & Scott Maestol). The same source also credits the Crash Team, in the same breath, as both the reigning side Omega defeated at King of the Ring AND (elsewhere on the same page) "the three time North American Tag Team Champions" — an internal ambiguity in the fed's own period text about which belt(s) the Crash Team actually held; not resolved into a separate Crash Team reign row on this ledger pending a cleaner receipt. See review-queue.json's own iwf-tag-team entry.
